newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish builder to invest IPO revenue in production.
newsitem.headline: Polish builder to invest IPO revenue in production.

text.p: Polish construction and engineering firm Elektromontaz Warszawa SA, whose initial public offering starts later this month, plans to invest the issue's proceeds in modernising production.

"We will invest the revenue to modernise our machines...and expand our production, which is the most profitable part of our activities," Elektromontaz Warszawa's President Wojciech Stelmach told a news conference on Wednesday.
Elektromontaz's IPO of between 1.4 and 1.75 million new shares at a minimum price of 3.5 zlotys will take place from November 18 to November 23.
Stelmach said the firm would announce next week whether it would seek an underwriter for the issue.
He said Elektromontaz, 81.3-percent owned by Mostostal Export, needed the capital increase because it did not use credit to finance investment.
The firm plans to enter the Warsaw bourse's parallel market and later move to the exchange's main floor.
It plans to invest a total of 9.4 million zlotys from 1996 to 2000 and has already invested about two million zlotys this year from its own funds.
Mostostal Export President Karol Nachtlicht, also present, said his firm planned to maintain its controlling stake in Elektromontaz.
"We want to have at least a 51 percent stake in Elektromontaz Warszawa," he said.
Elektromontaz, which netted 1.4 million zlotys on sales of 42.4 million zlotys last year, expects to earn 1.8 million zlotys in 1996 on sales of 51.4 million zlotys.
Its other shareholders are the state treasury, with 16.27 percent, and management, with 2.44 percent of the company's existing 6,915,500 shares, all approved for public trade.
